results.gate: A4 sign convention fixed by measurement, not by intuition
results.detail:
uniform-K anchor reproduces sqrt(k_par/k_perp) to 1.52%
K = exp[-alpha C], alpha > 0 (the brief's sign): the response along
  the channel relative to across it is 0.9914 < 1 -- gravity is WEAKER
  along the line joining the wells and stronger transverse to it.
K = exp[+alpha C]: 1.0072 > 1 -- this is the sign that makes the
  response STRONGER ALONG THE CHANNELS.
Both are implemented as sign=-1 and sign=+1 and both are scanned in
the mechanism map.  The naive argument (a poorer conductor needs a
larger gradient) is wrong here because flux can be diverted; it is
right only where no diversion is possible, i.e. for a radially aligned
K in spherical symmetry, which is the regime the shell-averaged
boost lives in.
